Results for the realistic capacity soak fixture after the store
read-path work of issue #196: pooled read-only loads, batched public
Schedule and Display Snapshot queries, bulk Display status loads, and
the revision-keyed public Schedule and Crew Rundown memos.

Captured on the same workstation as
capacity_realistic_baseline.txt, with the command that file
documents:

  go test ./internal/server -run '^$' \
    -bench 'BenchmarkCapacityRealistic' -benchtime=1x -benchmem -count=8

benchstat against the baseline reports, at -benchtime=1x (every
sample a cold build against a fresh fixture):

  PublicScheduleDirect         -92.68% sec/op  -74.41% B/op  -82.89% allocs/op
  CrewRundownLoad              -48.85% sec/op        ~ B/op        ~ allocs/op
  DisplaySnapshotFanoutAfter-
  Publish                      -51.82% sec/op   -6.14% B/op  -24.67% allocs/op

CrewRundownLoad keeps its allocation count because its loader was
already batched: what changed for it is that it no longer queues
behind the single writer connection, and it now reads one extra
revision row to decide whether its memo is current.

PublicScheduleRepeat is new and has no baseline. It measures the
second and later attendee requests at one Schedule stream cursor
(10.40m sec/op, 9.348k allocs/op) against PublicScheduleDirect's cold
build in the same run (19.32m sec/op, 45.87k allocs/op). The Crew
Rundown memo is not visible here because these runs are cold by
construction; measured in process, a repeated Crew Rundown load at an
unchanged revision falls from about 7.3ms to about 40us.

The wall-clock figures carry the same caveat as the baseline: an
ordinary workstation under background load, useful for comparison on
the same machine rather than as a certified objective. Note also that
the baseline's own variance is very wide on two of these rows (65%
and 101%), which is itself a symptom of what this ticket removed:
read traffic contending for the writer connection.

goos: linux
goarch: amd64
pkg: github.com/dotwaffle/beamers/internal/server
cpu: AMD Ryzen 5 3600 6-Core Processor
